verified: CPO's public mask builder loads model.state_dict() and defines float_keys as every shared floating state-dict key; it does not first restrict keys to model.named_parameters().
The same builder carries prior accumulated mask entries forward wholesale and extracts reference weights from cur_sd for any retained key present in the state dict.

CPO's public CLGRPOTrainer applies the regularizer by iterating raw_model/unwrapped_model.named_parameters() and checking whether each parameter name exists in the importance mask. Mask keys that are not trainer-visible parameter names therefore have no gradient-consumption path in this trainer.
PyTorch's Module contract states that state_dict contains parameters plus persistent buffers, while named_parameters(remove_duplicate=True) removes duplicated Parameter objects by default.

An independent local PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu sanity fixture with one Linear module registered twice plus one persistent floating buffer produced state_dict keys ['buf','a.weight','b.weight'], default named_parameters ['a.weight'], and named_parameters(remove_duplicate=False) ['a.weight','b.weight']. This reproduces the namespace divergence mechanism in a minimal runtime fixture.
scope: This verifies the public-release namespace mismatch premise: state-dict-only persistent buffers and duplicate alias names can be eligible for mask serialization even though the trainer consumes only canonical named_parameters entries.
It does not establish that the released Qwen3-VL checkpoints actually contain a material number of such dead aliases/buffers, nor quantify real mask-file/RSS/runtime savings.

The independent toy fixture ran on PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, not the worker's requested PyTorch 2.8.0/full-Qwen/DeepSpeed environment. The PyTorch API semantics are documented, but exact 2.8/full-model byte-level reproduction remains open.

The worker's canonical trainer-namespace repair and six-case invariance matrix were not independently re-executed in this audit. They remain worker-local synthetic repair evidence rather than primary-source behavior.

Filtering by canonical parameter name is semantically conservative only for the current trainer contract. A future consumer that intentionally uses persistent buffers or noncanonical aliases would require a new explicit contract rather than inheriting this conclusion.
downstream_implication: The public CPO release has a mechanically verifiable producer/consumer namespace mismatch: masks are produced from the broader state_dict namespace but consumed through named_parameters. A production cleanup may safely target only keys proven outside the exact trainer-consumed namespace, but real-model savings and repair invariance still require pinned PyTorch/full-model reproduction before being treated as measured benefit.
exact_next_action: On a future continual-learning audit, rerun the exact canonical-namespace fixture under PyTorch 2.8.0 and a smallest real tied Transformers model; only then bind any measured mask-byte/RSS/build-time benefit to the public CPO release.
